lang_en:
We had a week off in December.
I wanted Pahalgam.
She wanted Gulmarg.
Neither of us budged.
So she opened NakshIQ.
And turned the phone to me.
Gulmarg in December. Ten out of ten.
Its busiest month, too.
Pahalgam. Skip.
Gulmarg it was.
First morning, her hand in my jacket pocket.
I told her she was right.
Just the once.
Travel intelligence is an answer you can just show.
NakshIQ.
lang_hi:
दिसंबर में हमारे पास एक हफ़्ते की छुट्टी थी।
मुझे पहलगाम जाना था।
उसे गुलमर्ग।
दोनों में से कोई नहीं माना।
तो उसने NakshIQ खोला।
और फ़ोन मेरी तरफ़ घुमा दिया।
दिसंबर में गुलमर्ग। दस में से दस।
और सबसे भीड़ वाला महीना भी।
पहलगाम। स्किप।
तो गुलमर्ग तय हुआ।
पहली सुबह, उसका हाथ मेरी जैकेट की जेब में।
मैंने मान लिया कि वो सही थी।
बस एक बार।
ट्रैवल इंटेलिजेंस मतलब, ऐसा जवाब जो बस दिखा दो।
NakshIQ.
shots: s1: Apartment living room, morning: the man and woman (late 20s) on a sofa, each holding a phone and shaking their head at the other, a half-smiling standoff.
s2: Close-up, same room: the woman taps her phone, screen glow on her face, the screen never visible to camera.
s3: She turns the phone toward him, screen out of focus; his stubborn look softens into a reluctant grin.
s4: Gulmarg, morning: the two step out of a wooden hotel door in winter jackets onto open mountain slopes, no one else in frame.
s5: Close-up: her gloved hand slips into his jacket pocket and his hand closes around it.
s6: Wide: the two stand side by side facing the Gulmarg mountains; he says something, she laughs and nudges his shoulder.
